elaine: Heads-up: during a load test the onboarding flow produced duplicate side-effects again. Looks like token refresh + near-simultaneous retries from different SDK clients.
omar: Ugh. Any traces?
elaine: Short trace: `REQ id=onb_99 status=429 refresh_started=true retry=1` then `REQ id=onb_99 status=200 side_effect=applied` from a separate connection ~300ms later. No Idempotency-Key in the sampleapp requests.
yuki: Are we seeing jitter alignment across runtimes? Last time node used full-jitter and go used fixed exponential, they lined up under load.
omar: I pulled timing histograms: many retries clumped at ~250-400ms. Go's default max backoff was too low.
elaine: Two proposals: 1) sampleapp should auto-add an Idempotency-Key for POSTs unless explicitly disabled. 2) SDKs should provide a built-in "token-refresh-guard" so retries wait for an in-progress refresh to finish (or stagger).
yuki: I like the guard. Implementation idea: SDK keeps a refresh mutex per credential, and retries that observe refresh_in_progress wait a randomized delay (rand(0, min( backoff, 300ms ))) before executing, to avoid thundering on refresh completion.
omar: That pairs well with decorrelated jitter for backoffs. Can we standardize on a named profile: "prod-defensive" with attempts=5, base=120ms, cap=2s, strategy=decorrelated-jitter?
elaine: Sounds good. Also add an opt-out env var RW_RETRY_PROFILE=legacy|prod-defensive so integrators can keep old behaviour temporarily.
yuki: For sampleapp idempotency token, let's use `Idempotency-Key: rnd-<uuidv4>` created per user-flow and persisted in the client state until flow completes. Make it toggleable via SAMPLEAPP_IDEMPOTENCY=on/off.
omar: Tests: add an integration that simulates a short-lived auth server (TTL 1s) and asserts no duplicate side-effects under parallelism. Also add unit tests that confirm the refresh-guard actually defers retries while refresh is in-flight.
ci-bot: CI:created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-common/issues/450 for refresh-guard spec (auto).
elaine: Who can own changes? I'll take the sampleapp patch and doc blurb. Omar take SDK core guard and go/python clients. Yuki can do node SDK and tests.
omar: Ack. I'll draft a thin API: `client.setRetryPolicy({ profile: 'prod-defensive', refreshGuard: true })` and a small helper `withIdempotency(key, fn)` in SDKs for common flows.
yuki: I'll also add a telemetry counter `retries.post_refresh_wait` and `side_effects.duplicates` so we can track regressions.
ci-bot: CI: PR opened https://github.com/redwood-inference/sampleapp/pull/823 by elaine - checks running.
elaine: Once merged, we'll flip default in SDKs after one release cycle. For now shipping as opt-in avoids surprising integrators.
omar: One more thing: add a short FAQ entry in onboarding: "Why we add Idempotency-Key and when you might disable it". Keep it friendly.
yuki: Ok I'll coordinate cross-repo PRs. If anyone sees more duplicates please @here and paste traces.
elaine: Thanks team :thumbsup:
